comparisons.evidence: P covers additional causal mechanisms such as emotional avoidance ("Route around fear"), comprehension ("Purpose transparency"), uncertainty reduction ("Appointment rehearsal"), and lateness recovery ("same-day recovery queue"). Q's eight survivors are well consolidated but somewhat narrower.

P reaches unusual territory with a "maximum wait guarantee" and appointments as a "transferable reservation"; Q is comparably inventive with a "care failover ladder" and a "reliability reciprocity contract".

Q explicitly derives ideas from named rules such as "Graceful degradation", "Redundancy", and "Virtual queues", then carries graceful degradation into the finalist "Care failover ladder". P only offers a loose analogy: "Airlines, restaurants, and ticketing systems manage capacity dynamically".

Both select essentially the strongest practical mechanism: P's "Soft cancellation plus automatic alternatives" and Q's "readiness handshake plus slot liquidity" identify uncertainty early, preserve access, and recover otherwise wasted capacity.

Q states concrete assumptions and failure modes for every survivor, including "Arrival bunching", "Gaming, excessive offer messages", "Privacy concerns", and the hospital being "unable to honour its commitment". P mainly supplies ratings and benefits, with few explicit ways its proposals could fail.

Q repeatedly names precise causal insights, especially "an 'unsure' patient is not yet a no-show. It is a recoverable state" and "The true scheduling unit may be the household". P has good insights—such as reframing a slot as a "transferable reservation"—but articulates them less consistently.

note: P has the broader mechanism spread; Q is substantially stronger in disciplined cross-domain transfer and explicit adversarial critique.
